title: Bill Bellamy to Receive Icon Award at Whats Funny Comedy Festival, Co-Founded by Lil Rel Howery
description: Comedian, actor, and entertainer Bill Bellamy will be presented with the Icon Award at the 2026 Whats Funny Comedy Festival, recognizing his decades
body:
Comedian, actor, and entertainer Bill Bellamy will be presented with the Icon Award at the 2026 Whats Funny Comedy Festival, recognizing his decades of excellence and impact on stand-up comedy and entertainment.

	The Whats Funny Comedy Festival was co-founded by Knowledge Beckom and Lil Rel Howery (“Get Out,” “Rel,” “Vacation Friends 2”) with the mission to spotlight Black and Brown comedians and make Chicago the “next great home of comedy discovery.”
	

	The festival’s upcoming third edition will be held September 19-26 at venues throughout Chicago, including Comedy Bar, Laugh Factory, Bellagio 223, ETA Theater, and Wax Vinyl Bar. More than 50 comedians from 20 cities will perform in showcases, including Cousin Tiera, Correy Bell, Eva Evans, Rich Thomas, Shang and Chris ‘CP’ Powell, host of the latest reboot of BET’s “Comic View.”


	On Sept. 21, Bellamy will receive the Icon Award during the inaugural Whats Funny Today Show Chicago Comedy Legends ceremony. Bellamy will be honored alongside 15 Chicago comedians whose careers helped shape the city’s comedy legacy. The celebration will conclude with a live taping of the “Whats Funny Today Show” podcast featuring Bellamy and special guests.

	Another one of the week’s marquee events will be the live taping of Howery’s next stand-up comedy special on Sept. 20; his previous special, “Rel Talk,” was filmed during the inaugural Whats Funny Comedy Festival and released on Tubi last year. Howery will also lead a master class, sharing insights from his journey through stand-up, television and film. 

	“The Whats Funny Comedy Festival was created to celebrate the incredible legacy of Black comedy while creating meaningful opportunities for today’s comedians to learn, perform, and build lasting careers,” Beckom, the festival’s co-founder and executive director, said in a statement. “Every year we strive to elevate the experience for audiences and performers alike, and 2026 will be our biggest and most impactful festival yet.”
	

	For the full schedule, tickets and additional information, visit the Whats Funny Comedy Festival website.

schema.headline: Bill Bellamy to Receive Icon Award at Whats Funny Comedy Festival, Co-Founded by Lil Rel Howery

title: Boxing Legend Chris John Joins Silver Media Group for Animated Series ‘Dragon’s Dojo’ (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Singapore’s Silver Media Group has signed a memorandum of understanding with Indonesian boxing legend Chris John to develop “Dragon’s Dojo,” a mobil
body:
Singapore’s Silver Media Group has signed a memorandum of understanding with Indonesian boxing legend Chris John to develop “Dragon’s Dojo,” a mobile-first vertical animated series drawing on Indonesian folklore. 

	The project marks the first chapter of the ASERYA Asian Mythology Franchise.

	The venture unites Silver Media Group with Chris John, longtime Indonesian TV executive Harun Kurniawan and Koollab Studios as co-production partners.
	

	“Dragon’s Dojo” launches the ASERYA Universe, an interconnected Asian mythology franchise spanning animation, comics, games and merchandise. The universe pairs real-world figures with young protagonists, folklore and mythical beings drawn from across the continent, with the goal of introducing Asian stories to global audiences.


	The story follows ancient creatures appearing in the modern world, prompting heroes from different countries to confront a rising darkness threatening the region. In “Dragon’s Dojo,” Chris John takes on an animated alter ego, cast as the head instructor and mentor at the show’s namesake martial arts academy, which works with young people facing hardship. As creatures from Indonesian mythology emerge to threaten his students’ community, Chris and his pupils find their fight extends beyond monsters to their own inner struggles.

	The series is designed as a multi-platform franchise with potential extensions into comics, games and merchandise.

	Chan Gin Kai, founder and CEO of Silver Media Group, said Asia holds some of the richest histories, cultures and mythologies in the world, but many of these stories remain little known outside their home countries.
	

	“With ASERYA, we want to build an interconnected universe where these stories can come alive for a new generation of audiences,” Chan said. “‘Dragon’s Dojo’ is the beginning of that journey in Indonesia, combining the legacy of a true champion in Chris John with the power of mythology, action and values-driven storytelling. As we open the door to a wider universe of stories from across Asia, we hope to share this rich heritage with the world.”

	Chris John said martial arts involves more than learning how to fight, teaching discipline, respect, courage and how to face life’s challenges. “Throughout my career, boxing has taught me that the greatest victories are not only achieved in the ring, but also in overcoming the challenges we face every day,” he said. “‘Dragon’s Dojo’ brings these values into an exciting adventure where young people can discover their strength, purpose and the courage to find their own path while experiencing the richness of Indonesian mythology.”

	Kurniawan said Indonesia has extraordinary stories, legends and cultural heritage passed down through generations. “‘Dragon’s Dojo’ gives us an opportunity to bring these elements into a contemporary format and introduce them to audiences around the world,” he said. “We are creating something that is proudly Indonesian while being part of a much larger Asian storytelling universe.”

	Koollab Studios co-founder Oliver Guse said the future of entertainment will be shaped by the collaboration between human creativity, technology and new approaches to storytelling. “At Koollab Studios, we believe innovation should empower creators to tell bigger and more ambitious stories while preserving the authenticity and emotional heart that make them meaningful,” Guse said. “‘Dragon’s Dojo’ represents an exciting opportunity to combine creative vision with new production possibilities, bringing Indonesia’s rich culture and mythology to audiences around the world.”

	“Dragon’s Dojo” is in development, with production and release details to be announced.

	Silver Media Group, founded by Golden Horse Award-winning producer Chan Gin Kai, manages a portfolio of more than 1,500 intellectual property assets spanning film, animation, games and graphic novels. The company has partnered with a fund manager licensed by the Monetary Authority of Singapore to establish the Silver Media Fund, an institutional-grade media investment vehicle focused on developing and financing scalable IP.
	

	Koollab Studios was co-founded by Guse, who has spent three decades working in animation production, and focuses on production workflows built around emerging technologies.

schema.headline: Boxing Legend Chris John Joins Silver Media Group for Animated Series ‘Dragon’s Dojo’ (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Ella Langley’s ‘Choosin’ Texas’ Spends 17th Week at No. 1, Now Solely Holds Fourth Place Spot Among All-Time Hot 100 Streaks
description: Ella Langley‘s “Choosin’ Texas” is unquestionably the biggest hit single of the year, and all that’s left to decide is where the seemingly unstoppab
body:
Ella Langley‘s “Choosin’ Texas” is unquestionably the biggest hit single of the year, and all that’s left to decide is where the seemingly unstoppable song ultimately lands among the biggest chart hits of all time. The country crossover smash just landed its 17th week at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100, which gives it still more bragging rights, as the tune is now in sole possession of the No. 4 spot on the list of historic chart-topping streaks.
	

	As of last week, “Choosin’ Texas” was tied with three other songs that had also landed 16 weeks at No. 1: Morgan Wallen‘s “Last Night,” Luis Fonsi & Daddy Yankee’s “Despacito” and Mariah Carey and Boys II Men’s “One Sweet Day.” Now that she has left those songs in the dust, there are just three more tunes to surpass to set an all-time record: Lil Nas X’s “Old Town Road” and Shaboozey’s “A Bar Song (Tipsy),” each of which was No. 1 for 19 weeks, and Carey’s “All I Want for Christmas,” the all-time record-holder with 22 weeks on top. Not long ago, it would have seemed impossible to imagine anyone edging past Carey’s holiday perennial, but with the roll Langley is on, another six weeks at No. 1 is not a laughable goal.


	One reason to think that “Choosin’ Texas” may not be slowing down much, if at all, on its march toward setting further records: it just reached the top 10 on Billboard’s pop airplay chart for the first time this week, as stations that would have never, ever played a traditional country song find themselves giving in to audience demand. Overall radio play for the song was up 4% for the week, because of the added pop play, according to Billboard.
	

	Langley landed another week at the top despite a strong showing from Ariana Grande, who has two songs in the top 10 as a result of the “Petal” album’s release. Leadoff single “Hate That I Made You Love Me,” which debuted on top when it came out in May, jumped back up from No. 8 to No. 2. One other song from the new set made it into the upper ranks: “Petal,” the album’s title track, debuted at No. 4.

	Of course, the Grande resurgence means that country songs do not occupy all five of the chart’s top spots, as they did on last week’s historic chart. But the representation for the genre is barely diminished. Wallen’s “Been by Now” dropped just one position, to No. 3, in its second week out. Taylor Swift’s “I Knew It, I Knew You” fell two spots to No. 5. Stella Lefty’s freshman smash “Boston” dropped a single spot to No. 6. The Wallen/Langley duet “I Can’t Love You Anymore” dropped three slots to No. 7. And Langley’s “Be Her” slipped one spot to No. 10.

	Obviously, there is not much room in the top 10 at present for anyone who is not either a country star or Ariana Grande. But two songs that don’t fit either of those criteria made the grade. “Dracula” by Tame Impala and Jennie is at No. 8, down two spots from last week, and Olivia Dean’s “So Easy (to Fall in Love)” is right behind it at No. 9, also down two slots.

	While Grande wasn’t able to surge past Langley to reclaim the No. 1 spot on the Hot 100, she does own the top position on the Billboard 200 album chart with “Petal,” as reported Sunday. (Langley’s “Dandelion” album is No. 4 on that chart.)

	This week’s metrics for “Choosin’ Texas,” as reported by Billboard, add up to 24.9 million official streams (down 2% for the week) and 54.5 million radio airplay audience impressions (up 4%)..

	If “Choosin’ Texas” manages to go the distance and somehow beat “All I Want for Christmas” as the all-time leader in weeks at No. 1, it may be a short-lived victory, of course, since the Carey song has tended to go No. 1 for a few weeks every December in recent years. But who knows — at this rate, listeners could yet choose Texas over Xmas.

schema.headline: Ella Langley’s ‘Choosin’ Texas’ Spends 17th Week at No. 1, Now Solely Holds Fourth Place Spot Among All-Time Hot 100 Streaks

title: What to Know About Tupac’s Murder Trial and Suspect Duane ‘Keffe D’ Davis
description: For three decades, rap legend and cultural icon Tupac Shakur’s killing has remained one of America’s great unsolved mysteries, spawning countless bo
body:
For three decades, rap legend and cultural icon Tupac Shakur’s killing has remained one of America’s great unsolved mysteries, spawning countless books, documentaries and long-form investigative journalism pieces. Now, the man accused of orchestrating his 1996 shooting is finally headed to trial with his memoir, as well as a Netflix docuseries on Diddy, serving as key evidence.

	Jury selection began on Monday in the case against Duane “Keffe D” Davis, 63, who is facing one charge of murder with a deadly weapon with the intent to promote, further or assist a criminal gang in Shakur’s death. Prosecutors allege Davis both ordered the killing of Shakur and provided the murder weapon. (Davis has maintained his innocence.)
	

	On the night of Sept. 7, 1996, Shakur was shot four times with a Glock .22 pistol while his car was stopped at a red light in Paradise, Nev. The bullets came from a white Cadillac that had pulled up alongside Shakur’s vehicle — which was being driven by his label boss, Marion “Suge” Knight — and struck the hip-hop artist in the chest, arm and thigh, while one of the bullets grazed Knight in the head. Shakur succumbed to his injuries six days later.

	Police arrested Orlando “Baby Lane” Anderson, a member of the South Side Crips gang, on Oct. 2 in connection with the shooting — only to release him the same day without being charged. Shakur and his entourage had attacked Anderson in the lobby of the MGM Grand in Las Vegas on the night of Sept. 7, mere hours before the shooting, after an affiliate of Shakur’s (and member of the rival Mob Pirus Bloods gang) recognized Anderson as someone who’d attempted to rob him. Two days after the shooting, on Sept. 9, the South Side Crips and Mob Pirus Bloods engaged in an all-out gang war that culminated in three deaths, and Anderson was shot in the leg and confined to a wheelchair. On Sept. 12, Shakur’s mother, Afeni, filed a wrongful death suit against Anderson, which was settled before Anderson perished in another gang shooting in 1998.
	

	Though Anderson has long been suspected of being the gunman who fired the fatal shots that killed Shakur, his uncle, Davis, who was seated in the white Cadillac, had also been implicated in the drive-by shooting. Greg Kading, a former LAPD detective who’d participated in the task force that investigated the murders of Tupac Shakur and the Notorious B.I.G., self-published the 2011 book “Murder Rap: The Untold Story of the Biggie Smalls & Tupac Shakur Murder Investigations,” which not only implicated Sean “Diddy” Combs in the killing of Shakur, owing to the East Coast-West Coast hip-hop rivalry, but also included portions of a taped interview Davis did with police in 2008 where he claimed Diddy had offered him $1 million to assassinate Shakur and Knight.

	“[Diddy] took me downstairs and he’s like, ‘Man, I want to get rid of them dudes…’ I was like, We’ll wipe their ass out quick, it’s nothing,” Davis said in the confession, according to Kading’s book.

	Davis subsequently spent years boasting about his purported role in Shakur’s killing. In 2018, to drum up anticipation for his upcoming memoir, he appeared in the BET docuseries “Death Row Chronicles,” where he discussed the night of Shakur’s murder, suggesting that the murder weapon was passed from someone in the backseat of the white Cadillac, but he wouldn’t say who. “Going to keep it for the code of the streets,” Davis remarked, adding, “It just came from the backseat, bro.”

	Davis released his memoir, “Compton Street Legend,” in 2019, whose intro stated, “I’m one of the only living eyewitnesses to Tupac’s killing,” before describing the night of Shakur’s killing in detail. In the book, Davis claims that he got a Glock and entered the white Cadillac with three others, looking for payback against Shakur and Knight for what they’d done to Anderson. “No words exchanged, the time for talking had passed, the shit was about to go down!” he wrote.

	The book continued: “Tupac made an erratic move and began to reach down beneath his seat. Pac pulled out a strap, and that’s when the fireworks started. One of my guys from the back seat grabbed the Glock and started bustin’ back.”

	According to The New York Times, a detective within the Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department who had been assigned to dig into the Shakur cold case stumbled upon Davis’ memoir and used it as evidence to build his case against him. “In 2023, he read aloud excerpts from the book to a grand jury, which ultimately indicted Mr. Davis on one count of murder in Mr. Shakur’s killing. Mr. Davis, 63, has pleaded not guilty and denied any involvement,” reported the Times.
	

	“Had he never decided to take money and go on BET and talk about this situation, had he decided to never write the book, he would not, probably, have ever been prosecuted for the crime,” Marc DiGiacomo, a prosecutor on the Davis case, said during a hearing last month.

	Meanwhile, Michael Sanft, a lawyer for Davis, has claimed that his client embellished many of the stories in “Compton Street Legend,” declaring during the hearing, “We’re putting way too much credence and value and weight on statements that are made for entertainment purposes only.”

	In addition to Davis’ memoir, there is the matter of “Sean Combs: The Reckoning,” a four-part docuseries directed by Alexandria Stapleton and produced by 50 Cent that was released Dec. 2 of last year on Netflix. The doc revealed that one year before Shakur’s killing, Diddy allegedly announced to “a whole room full of Crips” at a party that he would pay any amount for Shakur and Knight to be killed, and also re-aired portions of Davis’ interview with police — first circulated by Kading in “Murder Rap” — wherein he said Diddy met with him and offered $1 million to kill Shakur and Knight. (Diddy has denied any involvement in Shakur’s death.) Shakur’s estate filed a civil suit against Davis in April, alleging that grand jury transcripts and “Sean Combs: The Reckoning” have “revealed the existence of a broader, more complex conspiracy to murder Tupac that involved much more than mere retaliation for a prior altercation.”

	On July 18, 2023, the Las Vegas Police Department searched the home of Davis’ wife in Henderson, Nevada, in connection with the Shakur case and arrested him on Sept. 29 of that year. He’s been awaiting trial ever since, but is currently being held in Nevada’s High Desert State Prison on a separate conviction for a jailhouse fight, resulting in a sentence of 16 to 40 months. Experts believe that Davis’ trial for the killing of Shakur should last about a month and, although the death penalty is an option for first-degree murder convictions in Nevada, prosecutors will not be seeking it.

schema.headline: What to Know About Tupac’s Murder Trial and Suspect Duane ‘Keffe D’ Davis

title: Demi Lovato to Make ‘Camp Rock 3’ Cameo Appearance
description:
Demi Lovato will make a cameo appearance in “Camp Rock 3,” reprising the role of Mitchie Torres.

	The news comes just ahead of the Los Angeles prem
body:
Demi Lovato will make a cameo appearance in “Camp Rock 3,” reprising the role of Mitchie Torres.

	The news comes just ahead of the Los Angeles premiere event on Monday. The movie will debut on Disney Channel on Thursday before streaming on Disney+ beginning Friday.

	Previously, Lovato was announced to be executive producing without an on-screen role. Her return to the role of Mitchie comes 18 years after the original “Camp Rock” movie launched her career in 2008. Also returning to the franchise are the Jonas Brothers, who executive produce in addition to reprising their roles as brothers and Connect 3 bandmates Shane Gray (Joe Jonas), Nate Gray (Nick Jonas) and Jason Gray (Kevin Jonas). Maria Canals-Barrera also returns as Mitchie’s mother, Connie. 
	

	The official logline for “Camp Rock 3” reads, “When Connect 3 loses their opening act for a major reunion tour, they return to their beloved Camp Rock to discover the next big thing. As campers vie for the chance to open for their favorite band, tensions rise and friendships are tested — leading to unexpected alliances, revelations and romances.” Liamani Segura stars opposite Variety‘s recent Power of Young Hollywood honoree and cover star Malachi Barton. Along with Segura, Barton, Lovato and the Jonas Brothers, the cast includes Lumi Pollack, Sherry Cola, Hudson Stone, Casey Trotter, Brooklynn Pitts and Ava Jean. 


	Veronica Rodriguez directed “Camp Rock 3” from a screenplay by Eydie Faye. Executive producers include Tim Federle, Betsy Sullenger, Spencer Berman and Gary Marsh in addition to Lovato and the Jonas Brothers. Jamal Sims served as choreographer on the film, which was produced by Disney Kids & Family.
	

	“Camp Rock” premiered in 2008 as the second-most-watched Disney Channel Original Movie of all time, and remains No. 3 to this day, coming behind only “High School Musical 2” and “Wizards of “Waverly Place: The Movie.” It was followed by “Camp Rock 2: The Final Jam” in 2010, which was Disney Channel’s biggest movie that year. Together, the “Camp Rock” films have been watched for more than 535 million hours to date.

schema.headline: Demi Lovato to Make ‘Camp Rock 3’ Cameo Appearance

title: Damon Wayans Reunites With ‘In Living Color’ Co-Star David Alan Grier in ‘St. Denis Medical’ Season 3 Premiere
description: Damon Wayans will share the screen once again with his “In Living Color” castmate David Alan Grier with a guest appearance in the Season 3 premiere
body:
Damon Wayans will share the screen once again with his “In Living Color” castmate David Alan Grier with a guest appearance in the Season 3 premiere of “St. Denis Medical.”

	Wayans will play Dr. Highland, who is described as “a charming but pompous new doctor at St. Denis. He is filling in while Ron (Grier) is recovering from surgery. All the patients and staff, besides Alex (Allison Tolman) have fallen head over heels for him and his insights.” The episode will air on Nov. 2.
	

	“St. Denis Medical” is a mockumentary set in “an underfunded, understaffed Oregon hospital where the dedicated doctors and nurses try their best to treat patients while maintaining their own sanity,” per the official logline. The cast is led by Tolman, with Grier playing the grumpy emergency physician Ron. Wendi McLendon-Covey, Josh Lawson, Kahyun Kim, Mekki Leeper and Kaliko Kauahi also star. Justin Spitzer co-created the series with Eric Ledgin, who serves as showrunner. Both executive produce alongside Simon Heuer, Bridget Kyle and Vicky Luu. More Bees, Inc. and Spitzer Holding Company produce the series, while Universal Television is the studio.


	Grier was a cast member on all five seasons of “In Living Color,” which ran on Fox from 1990 to 1994, while Wayans starred in the first three seasons and recurred in Season 4. Wayans’ other best known credit is ABC’s “My Wife and Kids,” which he led alongside Tisha Campbell-Martin for five seasons from 2001 to 2005, and he more recently starred in Fox’s “Lethal Weapon” series for three seasons from 2016 to 2019. Wayans is repped by Verve.

schema.headline: Damon Wayans Reunites With ‘In Living Color’ Co-Star David Alan Grier in ‘St. Denis Medical’ Season 3 Premiere

title: Unscripted Producer Rachel Tung Renews ABC & Hulu Development Deal (EXCLUSIVE)
description:
Veteran unscripted producer Rachel Tung has renewed her development deal with ABC and Hulu, Variety has learned exclusively. 

	Under the renewed de
body:
Veteran unscripted producer Rachel Tung has renewed her development deal with ABC and Hulu, Variety has learned exclusively. 

	Under the renewed deal, Tung will continue developing original unscripted programming for Disney and serve as showrunner on select projects for ABC and Hulu. 

	Tung, who was formerly a vice president of unscripted at Paramount, developed and served as showrunner & executive producer on the first season of the popular Hulu reality series “Love They Nader.” That show followed model and actress Brooks Nader and her sisters as they try to break into the modeling industry in New York. The show debuted in August 2025 and was renewed for a second season later that year with Tung exiting as showrunner. 
	

	Tung was also the showrunner and executive producer on the second season of food and travel docuseries “Taste the Nation with Padma Lakshmi.” The show was nominated for outstanding hosted nonfiction series or special at the 2023 Emmy Awards. 


	Tung was also responsible for producing hit shows like “Hell’s Kitchen,” “Kitchen Nightmares,” and MTV’s “Deliciousness.” “Hell’s Kitchen” is preparing to enter its 25th season, while “Kitchen Nightmares” aired for seven seasons between 2007 and 2014 before Fox revived it for additional seasons beginning in 2023. “Deliciousness” served as a spinoff to the MTV series “Ridiculousness” and aired for three seasons at the basic cabler. 

	Tung has also produced in the true crime genre, including co-creating “Homicide Hunter” for Investigation Discovery. The show aired nine seasons beginning in 2011 and has become one of ID’s longest-running franchises, spawning the spinoff “Homicide Hunter: American Detective.” 
	

	Tung is repped by UTA.

schema.headline: Unscripted Producer Rachel Tung Renews ABC & Hulu Development Deal (EXCLUSIVE)

title: ‘Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma’: Hannah Einbinder and Jane Schoenbrun on the Future of Queer Cinema
description: Hannah Einbinder is optimistic about the future of queer cinema after starring in writer/director Jane Schoenbrun‘s latest film, “Teenage Sex and De
body:
Hannah Einbinder is optimistic about the future of queer cinema after starring in writer/director Jane Schoenbrun‘s latest film, “Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma.”

	“I hope that with the hopeful success of films like this, that [Hollywood] is able to trust queer filmmakers and showrunners more,” Einbinder told Variety at the U.S. premiere of “Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma” in Los Angeles on July 29.


	“Camp Miasma” debuted in limited release on Aug. 7, earning an impressive $251,000 from five screens and averaging $50,300 per location. Mubi will open the film, co-starring Gillian Anderson, in 50 new theaters next weekend before launching nationwide on Aug. 21.
	

	The movie is a tonal shift for Schoenbrun, whose 2024 sophomore feature “I Saw the TV Glow” is a dizzyingly psychological horror drama. With “Camp Miasma,” the filmmaker crafted a slasher comedy that is both spooky and funny.

	“I was going through a period of time that was really scary, but also really joyful,” Schoenbrun said. “And after the one-two punch of trauma that was ‘We’re All Going to the World’s Fair’ and ‘TV Glow,’ I was finally starting to feel good in my body and self, and so I think it represents a freer and more joyful part of my life.” 

	The film follows Kris (Einbinder), a queer filmmaker tasked with rebooting the in-universe “Camp Miasma” horror franchise. She becomes fascinated with the idea of recruiting Billy Presley (Anderson), the now-recluse star of the original film. Her pursuit of collaborating with the former ingenue takes her to the camp where the first “Camp Miasma” movie was filmed and where Billy now resides. 
	

	As Kris attempts to crack the origin story of Camp Miasma, the two embark on gory, sexy and campy romp in the woods. For all its lighthearted, sapphic fun, Kris faces her fair share of jump scares at the hands of Billy and Little Death (Jack Haven), the ghost behind the camp’s murders.

	Schoenbrun said that audiences being receptive to a “goofy” film was validating as a filmmaker. “I want to keep making things that explore and push at what I can do in the medium,” they said. “Every film I really want to feel unexpected in some way.” 

	“Jane is really smart and really intentional, while at the same time very collaborative,” said Jasmin Savoy Brown (“Yellowjackets”), who plays Mari, Kris’ partner. “That’s what’s really fun about working with filmmakers that aren’t seen: straight white men. Anyone outside of that binary, especially someone so outside of that binary, is going to have a different approach and different energy.”

	Even though “Camp Miasma” is more comedic than “TV Glow” and “World’s Fair,” that isn’t necessarily all Schoenbrun wants to see from queer films. “We put our antennas up as artists,” they said, “and whatever comes in, whatever it is, is what it should be.” 

	Patrick Fischler, who plays a harbinger-of-doom gas station attendant, called Schoenbrun a “super special human being,” and said he believes in their vision. “I want movies that everyone can relate to, so that we can open up the eyes and minds of a lot of close-minded people in the country, in the world,” Fischler said. “A movie like this can do it because it’s accessible, and it’s Jane’s vision. I just want more of this.” 



	

					The cast and crew of “Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma” — Graham Mason, Matthew Hyland, Kendra Terpenning, Patrick Fischler, Sepi Mashiahof, Gillian Anderson, Brigette Lundy-Paine, Eric Yue, Hannah Einbinder, Jane Schoenbrun, Willy McGee, Caddy Vanasirikul, Brandon Tonner-Connolly and Jasmin Savoy Brown — at the Los Angeles premiere.
									Gilbert Flores/Variety
	





	

					Hannah Einbinder reunites with her “Hacks” team — Jen Statsky, Lucia Aniello and Paul W. Downs — at the “Camp Miasma” Los Angeles premiere held at DGA Theater.
									Gilbert Flores/Variety
	





	

					Kristen Stewart and Hannah Einbinder pose at the “Camp Miasma” Los Angeles premiere after party.
									Gilbert Flores/Variety

schema.headline: ‘Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma’: Hannah Einbinder and Jane Schoenbrun on the Future of Queer Cinema

title: Jacob Elordi in Talks to Star in Ari Aster’s ‘Scapegoat’ With Scarlett Johansson
description: Academy Award nominee Jacob Elordi is in talks to star in Ari Aster‘s next film, A24’s “Scapegoat,” which already boasts fellow Oscar nominee Scarle
body:
Academy Award nominee Jacob Elordi is in talks to star in Ari Aster‘s next film, A24’s “Scapegoat,” which already boasts fellow Oscar nominee Scarlett Johansson leading the cast.

	The logline for the film is being kept under wraps, but there’s been plenty of early speculation about the plot. Some say the thriller is about a doctor who operates on an internet-famous person; others say it’s a sci-fi romance; and still others have described it as more of a traditional drama for Aster.
	

	Aster wrote and will direct the film, with Lars Knudsen producing for their Square Peg banner.


	News of Elordi’s casting comes during a big year for the Australian actor, known for his roles in HBO’s “Euphoria,” “The Kissing Booth” movies and “Saltburn.” He kicked off 2026 by earning an Academy Award nomination and a Golden Globe nod for his role in Guillermo del Toro’s “Frankenstein” for Netflix, as well as a second Golden Globe nod for the Prime Video limited series “The Narrow Road to the Deep North.” 

	While working the awards circuit, Elordi simultanteously embarked on the global press tour for “Wuthering Heights,” filmmaker Emerald Fennell’s take on the classic gothic romance. The Warner Bros. film — co-starring Margot Robbie, who also produced — was a box office hit, grossing over $240 million globally against an $80 million production budget.

	Then, this spring, Elordi wrapped up his tenure on “Euphoria” with the buzzy show’s third and final season. The actor will next star in Ridley Scott’s “The Dog Stars” for 20th Century Studios; the post-apocalyptic survival thriller, based on Peter Heller’s bestselling novel, will be released in theaters on Aug. 28. 
	

	Deadline first reported news of Elordi’s potential involvement in the project.

schema.headline: Jacob Elordi in Talks to Star in Ari Aster’s ‘Scapegoat’ With Scarlett Johansson

title: LISTEN: Summer Box Office Will Surpass the $4 Billion Benchmark
description: On today’s episode, in our Box Office segment, Variety’s Rebecca Rubin reports that the good news keeps on coming for the movie biz as “Spider Man:
body:
On today’s episode, in our Box Office segment, Variety’s Rebecca Rubin reports that the good news keeps on coming for the movie biz as “Spider Man: Brand New Day” soars in weekend two and “The Odyssey” becomes Christopher Nolan’s highest-grossing film. Most important, the summer tally to date has already hit the $4 billion benchmark that was the norm pre-COVID.

	Sony Pictures’ “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” packed ’em in for a second weekend. But it’s Universal Pictures’ “The Odyssey” that is defying gravity as an R-rated adult historical drama. The movie has legs that won’t quit, says Rubin, Variety‘s senior film reporter.
	

	” ‘The Odyssey’ now has made one point one billion dollars and it is officially Christopher Nolan’s highest-grossing movie of all time, and it’s also the highest-grossing Imax release ever. It has made $289 million just in Imax, and that’s above the company’s prior record holder, which was [2009’s] ‘Avatar.’ And that movie made around $270 million in Imax,” Rubin says. “And what’s significant about both of these milestones, both being Christopher Nolan’s biggest movie and Imax’s biggest movie, is this film has only been out for four weeks and it does not appear close to be slowing down. And so those numbers are just going to keep rising and keep rising.”

	Another accelerant is coming as “Odyssey” opens in China this week. 

	“China is a very big moviegoing market, and a lot of those Imax screens are sold out through September,” Rubin notes. “Christopher Nolan is a popular director there. And so just knowing the amount of hype that this film has already, the fact that it has already crossed the billion-dollar mark is going to generate a lot of excitement in China for this movie.”
	

	The heat from July’s two big releases, plus “Obsession” and “Backrooms” and other buzzy hits so far this summer is propelling the overall summer haul past $4 billion.

	“It’ll be the second time since the pandemic that summer revenues have hit that milestone. It used to regularly eclipse $4 billion pre-COVID,” Rubin says. “The only other time that Hollywood has earned $4 billion [in the summer] since the pandemic was in 2023, when Barbenheimer was all the rage. And here is we are only at August 10. And so this will firmly be the biggest summer since the pandemic.”

	(Pictured: “The Odyssey” and “Spider-Man: Brand New Day”)

description:
Rep. Lauren Boebert’s Son Tyler
                          Ex-Girlfriend Reported Him to Cops
body:
Rep. Lauren Boebert’s Son Tyler
                          Ex-Girlfriend Reported Him to Cops
                          Before Child Sexual Exploitation Arrest
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              August 10, 2026
                            8:28 PM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Rep. Lauren Boebert’s son Tyler Boebert’s ex-girlfriend showed cops a 43-second video he filmed of her ... which led to his arrest for child sexual exploitation, TMZ has learned. 
      
    
            Per a criminal affidavit, 21-year-old Tyler, who was arrested on August 9, was charged with child sexual exploitation to induce or entice, possession with intent, sexual exploitation of a child, sexual exploitation of a child involving video, and two additional counts related to contributing to the delinquency of a minor.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            The charges stem from an alleged video that a then-18-year-old Tyler filmed with his then-17-year-old girlfriend on April 1, 2024, who was reportedly turning 18 weeks after the video was shot. The ex-girlfriend reportedly called the police on April 2, 2024, after her ex was sent the video. 
      

            The affadavit also mentioned the alleged victim initially told the cops she was hesitant to report the incident ... because she didn't want Tyler to get in trouble.
      
    
            Tyler has yet to speak about the matter. 
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Rep. Boebert previously told TMZ, “I love my son.” 
      
    
            The politician added, “We take these allegations very seriously and pray for everyone affected during this challenging time." Tyler was released after posting a $10K bond. He will appear in court for a hearing later this month.

title: Beyoncé Dragged to Court Over Alleged Unauthorized Sample
description:
Beyoncé
                          Music Company Sues For Alleged Unauthorized 'Renaissance' Sampl
body:
Beyoncé
                          Music Company Sues For Alleged Unauthorized 'Renaissance' Sample
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              August 10, 2026
                            7:56 PM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Beyoncé is being dragged to court over an alleged unauthorized sample on her hit "Alien Superstar," TMZ has learned. 
      
    
            According to court docs, obtained by TMZ, a company called Hirose Enterprise and a producer named Shuji Hirose are suing Beyoncé and various music companies for alleged copyright infringement.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Hirose says it owns the rights to a song titled "Moonraker," performed by a musician named John Holiday. The company says Beyoncé sampled the “spoken-word introduction” of the song "Alien Superstar," which was released on her 2022 album "Renaissance."
      
    
            The suit claims Beyoncé and her team did not obtain a license at all for the use of the sample before the release ... but did obtain one weeks after the album release ... but only from the performer Holiday, who Hirose claims had transferred his entire interest in the song decades earlier.
      
    
            Hirose says it put Beyoncé’s company is on notice about the infringement but has continued to sell the record. The company is seeking an injunction to stop Beyoncé from continuing to make money off their work and for unspecified damages.

title: 'Phantasm' Star Reggie Bannister Dead at 80
body:
'Phantasm' Star Reggie Bannister
                          Dead at 80
                      
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Reggie Bannister, best known for battling the Tall Man throughout the "Phantasm" horror franchise, has died ... TMZ has learned.
      
    
            Reggie's wife, Gigi tells TMZ ... the actor died early Sunday morning at their cabin in Crestline, located in California's San Bernardino County mountains. She tells us Reggie was happy to be home during his final moments and died peacefully.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Gigi says Reggie was exposed to Agent Orange while serving in Vietnam and later battled Lewy body dementia and Parkinson's disease.
      

            Gigi says the family plans to hold multiple memorial services for relatives and friends, followed by a separate public celebration for Reggie's fans and fellow musicians.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            As we reported, Reggie's health had significantly declined in recent months, leaving his limbs stiff and making him essentially immobile. Gigi previously told us her own medical issues prevented her from safely lifting or transferring him, forcing the family to seek a full-time care facility.
      
    
            Reggie became a horror icon playing an ice cream vendor-turned-action hero across five "Phantasm" films, beginning with the 1979 cult classic. He was also a musician and frequently performed alongside Gigi.
      
    
            The couple met in 1995 after being introduced by actor Michael Berryman and married in 2001.
      
    
            Reggie was 80.
      
    
            RIP.
